title: The HashMap infinite loop in old JDKs
context: How could concurrent HashMap writes cause an infinite loop?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java collections questions (2 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: In Java 7 and earlier, resizing used head insertion for the linked list in each bucket. When two threads resized at the same time, the list could form a cycle. A later get on that bucket then looped forever, using CPU. Java 8 changed resize to keep the order of entries, which removes this cycle, but concurrent writes are still unsafe. The fix is the same: use ConcurrentHashMap.

points.title: Cycle during resize
points.why: Concurrent resizes in Java 7 could link a bucket into a loop.

points.title: Still not safe in Java 8
points.why: Java 8 fixed the loop, but concurrent writes can still lose data.
